Subject: Mutual Action Plan — Acme Maps PoC (recap & next steps)

Hi Jamie / Pat —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we have a working Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to move the PoC forward. Please reply with any corrections; otherwise we'll treat this as the agreed path.

Key pain points you shared
- Search and route attribution latency is causing degraded UX for mobile map loads (~600–900ms currently)
- High per-request GPU cost for nearest-neighbor queries at scale
- Lack of deterministic fallbacks when model variants are unavailable (failovers currently cause 10–15% error rate)

Goals (30–90 days)
1) Improve median map query latency to <= 250ms for 95% of mobile requests
2) Reduce per-query serving cost by 30% using batching/caching/quantization profiles
3) Run a 6-week PoC to validate integration and cost/latency gains, then move to a pilot for ~100k monthly queries

Stakeholders / decision process
- Jamie Liu (Head of Product) — final sign-off on UX/metrics
- Pat O'Connor (CTO) — technical & procurement sign-off
- Procurement committee (meets monthly; next meeting 2027-09-20) — contract and pricing approval

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (high level)
1) SOW & Pricing (Marissa / Rafael) — deliver draft SOW + pricing options by 2027-09-08
2) Legal review & Contract (Acme / Redwood legal) — target routing to procurement after 2027-09-09
3) Technical Kickoff & Integration (Logan / Acme eng) — schedule week of 2027-09-22
4) PoC Execution (2–6 weeks) — target PoC complete by 2027-10-15
5) Pilot decision & rollout planning — decision meeting target 2027-10-20

Attachments I'm sending: redwood-map-poc-sow.pdf (initial SOW draft), acme-mvp-requirements.xlsx (notes you shared + our interpretation).

Immediate asks / next steps
- Jamie/Pat: confirm the procurement meeting date (I heard 9/20), and whether the procurement package should include specific legal terms (standard Redwood EULA vs. enterprise amendment).
- Acme eng: share a small sample dataset and API keys for internal testing (can be redacted) — we'll use the sample to validate latency numbers during the PoC.
- Rafael: I've cc'd you to start pricing options (standard vs. committed reserved capacity).
- Logan: please draft a 1-pager onboarding runbook for the PoC (expected infra, network/VPC details, required endpoints).

Thanks — I'll follow up with an updated SOW and a compact MAP table after I hear back.

—
